reason: The text presents Jonathan as a model of putting others' welfare above his own interests and position. Despite being the crown prince with personal gain at stake, Jonathan prioritizes David's safety and well-being, making a covenant with him and sacrificing his royal status, armor, and weapons. His willingness to risk his life and inheritance to protect David—even against his own father—demonstrates that good character involves caring for others' welfare above self-interest. This contrasts sharply with Saul's paranoid, self-serving leadership that seeks to harm David out of fear. Jonathan's example illustrates that virtuous leadership is founded on selflessness and loyalty to others' welfare rather than personal power.
